scope: The PeakPickerHiRes TOPP wrapper (package P3-PICKER-TOOL of the early TOPP bundle): registration, the in-memory run, the parameter-failure and -write_ini behaviour. Sources and fixtures come from the independently versioned OpenMS4-cli, OpenMS4-topp and OpenMS4-test-data packages and are deliberately not resolved against the Core SDK checkout; the core PeakPickerHiRes sources are listed as context, because the picker itself is tests/data/peak_picking_provenance.json.
method: The wrapper is transcribed from the pinned C++ tool. The four in-memory registrations, the six parameter failures and TOPPWRITEINI_OVERWRITE are reproduced through cli::run_with in a per-case temporary directory. XML outputs are compared by decoded content (decision D6): counts, ids, levels, types and array names exactly, every m/z, retention time, intensity and float array value bit for bit, and the full decoded walk with exact numbers over container-neutral processing records. INI outputs are compared line by line with the ported FuzzyDiff and the registered whitelists.
evidence_tier: executed differential (tier 1): retained upstream outputs, and C++ outputs produced by the prebuilt product SDK (Debug, core 4fdec46, decision D7) recorded in the two oracle manifests below
upstream_test_definition: OpenMS4-tests/packages/test-data/topp/CMakeLists.txt lines 107-131 (the six parameter-failure tests, run on PeakPickerHiRes)

determinism: The picker is serial, as the source is. -threads 1, 2, 16 and 0 produce byte-identical output; the thread policy reaches the tool through ToolContext::thread_policy and is not consumed until the library offers a parallel pick_experiment.
target_verification: cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features mzml,paramxml --test topp_peak_picker_hi_res --lib on stable and 1.85.0 (ibmi dax); clippy --locked --all-features --all-targets -D warnings; doc --locked --all-features --no-deps; release builds of the PeakPickerHiRes binary with default features and with mzml,paramxml on both toolchains.
